patches.entity_key: Use of subjunctive after verbs of wish and desire
value: With the same subject, an infinitive is used instead of a que-clause
The que-clause must have a subject different from the main clause

evidence.notes: Both entries are the stated restriction and condition.

value: on is always third-person singular in agreement, even when it means 'we'
The senses 'we' and 'you' are informal and limited to spoken French
on cannot be used with plural verb forms

evidence.notes: First and third entries follow from the formation; the register limit comes from the listed informal uses.

patches.entity_key: Using -ci and -là to distinguish between two elements
value: Only used when two elements are contrasted; a single element needs no particle
The particle attaches to the noun, not to the demonstrative adjective
-ci marks proximity and -là marks distance

evidence.notes: All three entries follow from the rule's condition, word order, and trap.

value: Only when the agent is unspecified; if the agent matters, a passive with par is used
on requires a third-person singular verb form

evidence.notes: First entry follows from the passive-avoidance purpose; the second is the stated formation.

value: Limited to venir and its prefixed derivatives (devenir, prévenir, survenir, revenir)
The pattern does not apply to other -ir verbs with different stems

evidence.notes: Both entries follow from the rule's stated scope and the list of related verbs.

value: Agreement is with the antecedent pronoun after qui, not with c'est
The antecedent may be a stressed pronoun (moi, toi, lui), which determines the verb person
Applies to the c'est + pronoun + qui emphasis construction

evidence.notes: Derived from the stated agreement rule and the example sentences.

patches.entity_key: Verbs followed by preposition de before infinitive
value: The preposition de is required; à is not possible with these verbs
de becomes d' before a vowel

evidence.notes: First entry comes from the formation and trap; the elision is standard usage.

patches.entity_key: Verbs followed by preposition à before infinitive
value: The preposition à is required; de is not possible with these verbs
à contracts with the definite article (au, aux) when followed by a noun

evidence.notes: First entry comes from the formation and trap; the contraction is standard usage.

value: When the two subjects differ, a que-clause replaces the infinitive
No preposition (à or de) is inserted after these verbs

evidence.notes: First entry is the stated restriction; the second is the stated trap.

patches.entity_key: Verbs with avoir or être (six verbs)
value: Only these six verbs switch to avoir; other être verbs do not
The switch occurs only when a direct object follows the verb
With avoir, the past participle agrees with a preceding direct object

evidence.notes: All three entries follow from the rule's restriction, condition, and agreement rule.
